requirements.summary: 从实例联系样本点、有限样本空间与事件，辨别互斥并操作事件的并与交。
在有限等可能情形建立古典概型并求简单事件的概率。
由实例理解概率性质并运用事件概率的运算法则。
根据观察频率估计事件概率。
在有限样本空间解释两事件的独立性，用独立性计算古典概型概率。
了解从年鉴报表、调查、试验、普查抽样及网络等渠道获得数据的方法。
区分总体、样本和样本量，并认识数据的随机性。
用实例解释简单随机抽样流程，能用抽签和随机数抽取，并求样本均值、方差以认识样本与总体。
判断何时需要分层随机抽样，按比例分配样本量，并计算相应样本均值与方差。
按实际问题特征设计适当的抽样方法。
依据数据和任务选用统计图表，并理解恰当呈现的作用。
用样本估计总体的均值、中位数与众数，解释这些位置指标。
由样本估计标准差、方差与极差，并解释离散指标所表达的差异。
结合实例，从样本估计总体取值的规律。
用样本估计百分位数并解释其统计意义。
Translate a constrained optimization task into one variable and solve it.
Use polynomial, exponential, sine, cosine, square-root and reciprocal functions and their transformations to answer questions.
Infer parameters from contextual constraints.
Explain inversion using the square-root function, its graph, domain and range.
Differentiate polynomials, natural exponentials, sine, cosine, square root and reciprocal without aids; use the product rule.
Apply the chain rule to a natural exponential with a linear inner function.
Analyze functions and parameters in context with supplied or software-derived derivatives.
Model quantitative relations with simple sums, products or compositions of functions.
Describe exponential functions and explain the natural exponential's equality with its derivative.
Model bounded and unbounded growth or decay exponentially and assess model quality.
Interpret product sums as reconstructed totals or cumulative effects.
Explain signed areas in context.
Sketch an area-accumulation graph from the boundary function.
Explain and carry out the product-sum to integral transition using an introductory limit idea.
Explain geometrically and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus.
Use supplied antiderivatives and obtain polynomial antiderivatives without aids.
Apply interval additivity and linearity of integrals.
Reconstruct a total or cumulative effect from a rate or boundary function.
Use definite integrals to find areas.
Solve pure and applied problems with polynomials, the natural exponential and combinations of them.
Solve biquadratic equations, including without aids.
Reduce constrained extrema to a one-variable problem and solve it.
Use polynomial, exponential, sine, cosine, natural log and rational-power functions and their transformations.
Determine parameters from contextual constraints.
Interpret parameters in context and investigate their effects on families of functions.
Differentiate polynomial, exponential, sine, cosine, natural logarithm and rational-power functions without aids; apply both product and chain rules.
Study functions, including parameter dependence, with supplied or software-derived derivatives and antiderivatives.
Interpret the derivative through linear approximation.
Model quantities using sums, products and compositions of functions.
Describe exponential functions and explain why the natural exponential is its own derivative.
Model bounded and unbounded growth and decay exponentially and judge the fit.
Test invertibility, especially for natural exponential and log functions; obtain simple inverse formulas with domain and range.
Explain the geometric relation between the graphs of a function and its inverse.
Interpret a product sum as a reconstructed total or effect in context.
Interpret signed area in the setting of a question.
Construct an accumulation graph from a boundary function graph.
Explain and perform the limiting transition from product sums to the integral.
Justify the fundamental theorem using an intuitive idea of continuity and apply it.
Find polynomial antiderivatives unaided, use supplied primitives and use the natural log as a primitive of the reciprocal on its domain.
Use additivity over intervals and linearity of integrals.
Recover a total or accumulated effect from its rate or boundary function.
Use definite or improper integrals for areas and compute volumes of solids revolving about the horizontal axis.
Solve mathematical and applied problems using polynomial, exponential and composite functions, as well as sine and cosine.
Investigate properties of polynomial functions.
Investigate properties of exponential functions.
Investigate properties of the sine and cosine functions.
Investigate square-root and reciprocal powers.
Investigate how transformations affect the listed functions.
Analyze polynomials, the natural exponential and functions composed from them.
Interpret and determine parameters in the preceding functions.
Without aids, differentiate the listed polynomial, natural exponential, sine, cosine, square-root and reciprocal functions and use the product rule.
Use the product rule and the chain rule for a natural exponential composed with a linear function.
Investigate properties of polynomial functions.
Investigate properties of exponential functions.
Investigate properties of sine and cosine functions.
Investigate properties of the natural logarithm.
Investigate powers with rational exponents.
Investigate transformations of the listed families.
Analyze polynomial, exponential and composite functions as well as sine and cosine; investigate parameter-dependent properties.
Differentiate the specified polynomial, exponential, trigonometric, natural logarithm and rational-power families without aids, using product and chain rules.
Form and use a linear equation with one unknown to solve contextual problems.
Choose or construct the equation describing a stated situation.
Explain what parts of the equation or its solution mean in context.
Exploit algebraic structure when solving for the unknown.
Find the conditions giving zero, one or infinitely many solutions.
Solve one-variable linear equations fluently.
Use a linear function to formulate and solve contextual problems.
Select or construct a linear model of the relationship between two quantities.
Explain an input-output pair or a component of the function in its setting, drawing on structure as appropriate.
Interpret the function graph in the given context.
Connect symbolic, tabular and graphical forms of an abstract linear function.
Relate a contextual linear function's table, formula and graph.
Find and interpret a corresponding output or a possible input from the given representation in context.
Determine a linear rule from two pairs or from a pair and the rate of change.
Compute an output or recover an input corresponding to a specified output.
Solve contextual problems by constructing and using one linear equation in two variables.
Choose or construct an equation for a constraint involving two quantities.
Interpret the solution or components of the equation with reference to the situation.
Interpret the contextual graph of a linear equation in standard form.
Relate an abstract two-variable linear equation to its graph.
Relate a table to an equation or graph outside a contextual setting.
Connect the table, equation and graph when they represent a situation.
Use one given quantity to determine the other where a corresponding value exists.
Write a line equation from two points, a point and slope, or a point and a parallel or perpendicular line.
Formulate and solve contextual problems with two linear equations in two unknowns.
Choose or construct a system encoding two quantities and their constraints.
Use the algebraic structure to select a solution method for a two-variable system.
Decide when the system has no, one or infinitely many solutions.
Relate the equations of a system to their graph without a contextual setting.
Relate a system to its graph in an application.
Solve a two-equation linear system fluently.
Formulate and use one- or two-variable linear inequalities to solve context problems.
Choose or write linear inequalities for contextual constraints.
Interpret a coefficient, variable, term or solution in the situation, making use of structure.
Interpret a coordinate point in relation to the solutions of an inequality or system.
Derive a table, algebraic form or graph of linear inequalities from another representation.
